Subject: Residency commitments for APAC deployment

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the demo last week — TokyoTech is excited about Redwood's latency profile in APAC. Before we proceed to procurement, Legal and Infra need written confirmation on a few items related to data residency and cross-region processing. Can you please confirm the following in writing: 

1) Can Redwood guarantee that customer content (raw requests, model inputs/outputs) will be stored only within the APAC region we specify (region pinning) for the lifetime of the contract, excluding transient caches?
2) Under what circumstances would data be replicated to another region (e.g., backups, failover, analytics)? Are there controls to limit cross-region replication to only the same geopolitical area?
3) Do you provide a current subprocessor list and will Redwood contractually require subprocessors to adhere to the same residency restrictions?
4) Is there an addendum we can sign to the DPA to codify a non-export clause or an explicit carve-out for DR?

We need this documented for our privacy team and will share a target timeline for sign-off once we see it. If possible, please also include any limitations (e.g., logs, telemetry, operational traces) that might be excluded from the residency guarantee.

Thanks — Satoshi

--

Hi team / Satoshi — adding the technical context on region pinning and cross-region processing. I'll keep this high level for Legal and Infra reviewers.

Summary:
- Primary data at rest: For customers who opt into APAC region pinning (Private or Dedicated), customer content (inputs/outputs, stored artifacts) is persisted only on storage volumes located in the selected APAC region. That includes model caches persisted for longer than ephemeral TTL.

- Ephemeral caches and inference KV: We use edge routing and short-lived KV caches for latency-sensitive workloads. These caches are typically pinned to the nearest region but may be warmed from other regions during warm-up traffic; they are TTL-limited (usually seconds to minutes) and not considered "persistent storage."

- Backups and DR: We maintain encrypted backups for disaster recovery. By default backups are stored in a secondary region within the same cloud provider and are encrypted with customer-isolated keys for Private deployments. For APAC pinning we can configure backups to stay within the APAC geography (e.g., APAC-primary -> APAC-secondary) but we cannot guarantee same-zone replication across all cloud providers. In exceptional circumstances (global outage) we may enact cross-geography failover; that would be subject to contractual approval and pre-authorized runbooks.

- Operational logs / metrics / anonymized telemetry: These are aggregated and may be routed to central telemetry services for monitoring and capacity planning. We can offer a scoped retention policy and a suppression option for PII in logs for enterprise contracts, but aggregated metrics will generally be global.

Controls we can offer:
- Region pin flag on tenant config that prevents default cross-region store for persisted customer artifacts.
- Backup residency option (APAC-only backup mirrors).
- Pre-authorized DR playbook that requires customer opt-in before cross-geography failover.

Limitations / open items:
- Need to confirm whether TokyoTech considers operational logs (request/trace metadata) as in-scope for residency.
- We should align on acceptable recovery time objectives (RTO) if we limit cross-geography failover.

Happy to provide a short tech note for your infra team if helpful.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Satoshi Ito <s.ito@tokyotech.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Jul 2025 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency commitments for APAC deployment

Hi Satoshi / team — legal perspective here. We can accommodate a residency commitment with the following guardrails and proposed DPA language: 

1) Residency scope: Redwood will ensure that Customer Data (as defined in the DPA: inputs, outputs, and stored artifacts) is stored only within the mutually agreed APAC region for the duration of the agreement, subject to the exceptions below.

2) Exceptions (explicit and limited):
- Encrypted backups: Encrypted copies retained for DR may be stored in a secondary APAC region; cross-geography backups are only permitted with prior written consent for specific scenarios (eg. provider outage).
- Failover: Cross-geography failover is permitted only when the primary APAC region is unavailable and with an authorized DR activation process that includes customer notification.
- Legal compulsion: Redwood may disclose data if required by law, provided Redwood uses commercially reasonable efforts to notify Customer and limit scope.

3) Subprocessors: We will incorporate contractual commitments into our subprocessor agreements requiring adherence to the residency obligations to the extent possible. We will provide a current list and notify you of changes per the DPA notification timeline.

4) International transfers: For transfers out of the EU (if applicable) we will rely on SCCs or other lawful transfer mechanisms; for APAC customers we will propose region-specific clauses which will be added as an addendum.

5) Redlines: I can prepare a short addendum (one or two paragraphs) for the DPA that: (a) defines the residency requirement, (b) lists exceptions, and (c) specifies the DR notification and approval process. If accepted we can provide a DocuSign link for signature.

Question for TokyoTech: Do you require that operational telemetry or raw request logs are treated as "Customer Data" under the residency clause, or are those acceptable to remain in aggregated/global telemetry systems?

I'll draft the proposed addendum once we confirm the telemetry scope.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Legal — Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
